correctness.rationale: The theorem is proved for each integer \(n\geq2\) and every \(S>0\): zero irradiance cannot maximize; the stationary set is equal or n-1 low plus one high; the exact u(d)=d/(exp(d)-1) relation has strictly positive \(\nu''\) and exactly one fold for \(n\geq3\); second variation rejects the lower branch and third variation rejects its fold; the strict envelope derivative yields a unique global switching load; for n=2 the branch turns on continuously at \(S=4\). All candidate boundary and equality cases are included. verify.py executed from the new work package and passed 139189 numerical checks, not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Steele photoinhibition gives a physically motivated bell-shaped light-response model; the exact n-module allocation under forced total light is a natural benchmark. The theorem completely resolves a previously unidentified n-dependent optimization and establishes sharp qualitative separation of continuous and discontinuous transitions at n=3, an exact n=3 threshold and high-load allocation limit. It also states why excess-light disposal and dynamics invalidate direct hardware recommendations. The result is substantive mathematical structure, not a routine finite table or arbitrary parameter slice.
